cancer_detected.title: ⚠️ CANCER Detected - What to Do Next

steps.title: Don't Panic
steps.description: This requires medical confirmation. ONCOAi is a screening tool, not a diagnostic tool.
steps.action: Take a moment to compose yourself

steps.title: Schedule Urgent Appointment
steps.description: Contact an oral surgeon, maxillofacial surgeon, or ENT specialist as soon as possible (within 1-2 weeks)
steps.action: Call your dentist or doctor immediately for referral

steps.title: Gather Documentation
steps.description: Prepare the image and ONCOAi result to show your doctor
steps.action: Bring the uploaded image and this result to your appointment

steps.title: Professional Examination
steps.description: Doctor will perform visual examination and may use additional tools (endoscopy, ultrasound)
steps.action: Attend appointment and describe when you first noticed the lesion

steps.title: Biopsy If Recommended
steps.description: Doctor may recommend a biopsy for definitive diagnosis (gold standard)
steps.action: Undergo biopsy if recommended - results take 1-2 weeks

steps.title: Treatment Planning
steps.description: If confirmed, oncologist will discuss treatment options (surgery, radiation, chemotherapy)

cancer_detected.seek_emergency: Go to ER if you experience severe bleeding, difficulty breathing, or choking

suspicious_detected.title: ⚠️ SUSPICIOUS Result - What to Do Next

steps.title: Don't Worry - Schedule Check
steps.description: SUSPICIOUS means the lesion has features that warrant professional evaluation. It doesn't mean cancer.
steps.action: Schedule appointment with dentist within 1-2 weeks

steps.title: Document the Lesion
steps.description: Keep track of any changes: size, color, pain, bleeding
steps.action: Take notes and photos of changes (if any)

steps.title: Professional Evaluation
steps.description: Dentist or doctor will examine and determine if further testing is needed

steps.title: Follow Doctor's Advice
steps.description: Doctor may recommend: monitoring, biopsy, specialist referral, or treatment

steps.title: Regular Monitoring
steps.description: Even if benign, follow-up checks may be recommended

possible_causes: Benign lesions (aphthous ulcers, lichen planus, candidiasis)
suspicious_detected.timeline: 1-2 weeks for appointment, 1-2 weeks for biopsy results if needed

steps.title: Good News!
steps.description: The AI indicates no cancer-like features detected in this lesion.
steps.action: You can relax, but continue preventive care

steps.title: If Lesion Still Present
steps.description: If the ulcer/patch is still present, see dentist to determine cause (fungal, viral, bacterial, etc.)

steps.title: Prevention is Key
steps.description: Maintain healthy oral habits to prevent future issues
steps.action: Follow prevention tips: quit tobacco, limit alcohol, good hygiene

steps.title: Regular Monitoring
steps.description: Continue self-examination and routine dental visits
steps.action: Monthly self-exam, dental checkup every 6 months

steps.title: Seek Care If Changes
steps.description: If new symptoms develop or existing lesion worsens, get professional evaluation
steps.action: Don't ignore persistent symptoms - see dentist promptly

daily: Brush teeth twice daily with fluoride toothpaste
weekly: Check lips, tongue, inner cheeks, gums
Document any new or persistent lesions
monthly: Look for white, red, or speckled patches
Use ONCOAi if any concerning changes
annually: Ask dentist for oral cancer screening
